attributes.name: className
attributes.details: Supported Tailwind-style utilities, resolved entirely in Rust. See the engine README.

attributes.name: colors
attributes.details: Semantic theme-token overrides, scoped to NTheme and its descendants.

attributes.name: radius
attributes.details: Base radius in logical points, scoped to NTheme descendants.

attributes.name: selectable
attributes.details: Set false to exclude rendered browser text from selection and copying.

attributes.name: aria-activedescendant
attributes.details: Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox, group, or application.

attributes.name: aria-atomic
attributes.details: Indicates whether assistive technologies will present all, or only parts of, the changed region based on the change notifications defined by the aria-relevant attribute.

attributes.name: aria-autocomplete
attributes.details:
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be
presented if they are made.

attributes.name: aria-braillelabel
attributes.details: Defines a string value that labels the current element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

attributes.name: aria-brailleroledescription
attributes.details: Defines a human-readable, author-localized abbreviated description for the role of an element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

attributes.name: aria-checked
attributes.details: Indicates the current "checked" state of checkboxes, radio buttons, and other widgets.

attributes.name: aria-colcount
attributes.details: Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-colindex
attributes.details: Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-colindextext
attributes.details: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-colindex.

attributes.name: aria-colspan
attributes.details: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-controls
attributes.details: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

attributes.name: aria-current
attributes.details: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

attributes.name: aria-describedby
attributes.details: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

attributes.name: aria-description
attributes.details: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

attributes.name: aria-details
attributes.details: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

attributes.name: aria-disabled
attributes.details: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.

attributes.name: aria-dropeffect
attributes.details: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target. Deprecated. in ARIA 1.1

attributes.name: aria-errormessage
attributes.details: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

attributes.name: aria-expanded
attributes.details: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

attributes.name: aria-flowto
attributes.details:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

attributes.name: aria-grabbed
attributes.details: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation. Deprecated. in ARIA 1.1

attributes.name: aria-haspopup
attributes.details: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

attributes.name: aria-hidden
attributes.details: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

attributes.name: aria-invalid
attributes.details: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

attributes.name: aria-keyshortcuts
attributes.details: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

attributes.name: aria-label
attributes.details: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

attributes.name: aria-labelledby
attributes.details: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

attributes.name: aria-level
attributes.details: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

attributes.name: aria-live
attributes.details: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

attributes.name: aria-modal
attributes.details: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

attributes.name: aria-multiline
attributes.details: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

attributes.name: aria-multiselectable
attributes.details: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

attributes.name: aria-orientation
attributes.details: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

attributes.name: aria-owns
attributes.details:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

attributes.name: aria-placeholder
attributes.details:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

attributes.name: aria-posinset
attributes.details: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

attributes.name: aria-pressed
attributes.details: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

attributes.name: aria-readonly
attributes.details: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

attributes.name: aria-relevant
attributes.type: "text" | "additions" | "additions removals" | "additions text" | "all" | "removals" | "removals additions" | "removals text" | "text additions" | "text removals"
attributes.details: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

attributes.name: aria-required
attributes.details: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

attributes.name: aria-roledescription
attributes.details: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

attributes.name: aria-rowcount
attributes.details: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-rowindex
attributes.details: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-rowindextext
attributes.details: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

attributes.name: aria-rowspan
attributes.details: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-selected
attributes.details: Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.

attributes.name: aria-setsize
attributes.details: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

attributes.name: aria-sort
attributes.details: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.

attributes.name: aria-valuemax
attributes.details: Defines the maximum allowed value for a range widget.

attributes.name: aria-valuemin
attributes.details: Defines the minimum allowed value for a range widget.

attributes.name: aria-valuenow
attributes.details: Defines the current value for a range widget.

attributes.name: aria-valuetext
attributes.details: Defines the human readable text alternative of aria-valuenow for a range widget.

attributes.name: inputMode
attributes.details: Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

attributes.name: is
attributes.details: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

attributes.name: onKeyPress
attributes.details: Deprecated. Use `onKeyUp` or `onKeyDown` instead

attributes.name: onKeyPressCapture
attributes.details: Deprecated. Use `onKeyUpCapture` or `onKeyDownCapture` instead

attributes.name: blurTarget
attributes.details: Android source, outside this blur's foreground. Ignored by iOS and the browser.

attributes.name: enabled
attributes.details: Disable the effect while keeping children visible.

attributes.name: intensity
attributes.details: Blur strength from 0 to 100. Defaults to 50.

attributes.name: radius
attributes.details: Blur radius in logical points; overrides intensity (100 = 20 points).

attributes.name: autoPlay
attributes.details: Advance while visible and enabled. Pause this when the host screen loses focus.

attributes.name: indicatorColor
attributes.details: Overlay dot color (CSS). Default: the theme foreground.

attributes.name: indicatorGap
attributes.details: Space between overlay dots. Default: 8.

attributes.name: indicatorInset
attributes.details: Overlay dots' distance from the bottom edge. Default: 16.

attributes.name: indicatorPlacement
attributes.details: `overlay` draws the page dots over the slides instead of in a 44-point strip below them.

attributes.name: indicatorShadowColor
attributes.details: Soft shadow behind overlay dots (CSS).

attributes.name: interval
attributes.details: Milliseconds between slides. Default: 5000.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.details: Direction of swipe/paging; the same Rust state owns snapping and accessibility.

attributes.name: active
attributes.details: Pause rendering while retaining the surface for later use.

attributes.name: background
attributes.details: Surface clear color, independent of the theme background token.

attributes.name: entrancesReady
attributes.details: Hold new browser entrances at their starting pose while the host hides the surface. Defaults to true.

attributes.name: initialImageWaitMs
attributes.details: Keep the startup fallback until visible priority images have painted, for up to this many milliseconds.

attributes.name: onContentSizeChange
attributes.details: Intrinsic Rust content size, before the surface viewport clips or scrolls it.

attributes.name: onReady
attributes.details: Called once per surface after its first rendered UI snapshot.

attributes.name: overlays
attributes.details: Platform image/picker attachments positioned by Rust layout, keyed by node id.

attributes.name: scrollableOverlays
attributes.details: Attachments whose vertical drags scroll their engine viewport; native taps stay native.

attributes.name: scrollKey
attributes.details: Reset browser page scrolling when this navigation key changes.

attributes.name: serverFallback
attributes.details: Preserve server-rendered semantic content while the browser engine warms up.

attributes.name: settleInitialEntrances
attributes.details: Keep the first visible browser viewport settled when replacing already-visible server HTML.

attributes.name: stylesheet
attributes.details: Build-time stylesheet rules, resolved by the browser Rust layout backend.

attributes.name: colors
attributes.details: Semantic theme-token overrides, scoped to NTheme and its descendants.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.details: Seconds; default 1.4, clamped to 0.1..10.

attributes.name: run
attributes.details: Change this positive value to start another celebration. Zero is idle.

attributes.name: blurred
attributes.details: Use the theme's translucent presentation background inside the panel.

attributes.name: fitContent
attributes.details: Sheets fit Rust-measured content by default; false retains a fixed snap-point height.

attributes.name: showCloseButton
attributes.details: Hide the header button while retaining backdrop and swipe dismissal.

attributes.name: showsVerticalScrollIndicator
attributes.details: Hide the content's scroll indicator while preserving scroll gestures.

attributes.name: snapPoints
attributes.details: With content fitting, the first snap point limits the maximum sheet height.

attributes.name: children
attributes.details: Navigator/page content is retained. Routing belongs to the host app.

attributes.name: adaptQuality
attributes.details:
Whether "auto" judges the device by the frames now (default true). Pass false while what's on
screen isn't the game being played (a results card, a menu, a ready screen): their cost says
nothing about the game, and a level chosen there would be remembered for the next visit.

attributes.name: backdrop
attributes.details:
Static scenery behind `source` (a meadow, sky and hills; a board's backdrop): the renderer draws it
once into a cached image with this view's camera and light, and draws it again only when it
changes or the camera, light, size or quality do. Each frame then costs one full-screen image
instead of the whole scenery, and `source` is always drawn in front of it. It isn't stepped (its
velocities and animations stand still): call `backdrop.update(0)` after spawning or changing it.
Defaults to `source.backdrop`: a World's still entities (`still: true`, `backdropLayer`).

attributes.name: background
attributes.details: Screen/fog color: CSS or linear 0..1 RGB (alpha ignored). Defaults to NTheme's background, then dark navy.

attributes.name: camera
attributes.details: Mutate this object (e.g. `camera.eye`) from `onUpdate`; it is read every frame.

attributes.name: fog
attributes.details: Distance fog density towards `background` (e.g. 0.02). Default 0 (off).

attributes.name: onDrag
attributes.details: Finger down, moving and up (aiming, dragging pieces, slicing).

attributes.name: onError
attributes.details: GPU setup failures and rendering errors. Defaults to console.error.

attributes.name: onLongPress
attributes.details: A finger held still for half a second (pick up, show moves). No tap follows.

attributes.name: onOverlayTouch
attributes.type: ((phase: OverlayTouchPhase, x: number, y: number) => boolean | void)
attributes.details:
Touches for the overlay, in points in the view. Return true from "start" to claim the touch (a
button was hit): its moves and end come here, and the game gets no drag, tap or swipe for it.
"cancel" when the system takes the touch.

attributes.name: onPinch
attributes.details: Two fingers spreading, pinching or turning (zoom and rotate a board). Ends any drag in progress.

attributes.name: onPrimaryAction
attributes.details: Host primary action for keyboard input, such as Start/Stop or Play Again.

attributes.name: onStats
attributes.details: Called once a second.

attributes.name: onSwipe
attributes.details: A quick flick in one direction (2048, runners, sliding puzzles).

attributes.name: onTap
attributes.details: A quick tap, at `x, y` points in the view. `world.pick(x, y)` finds what was tapped.

attributes.name: onUpdate
attributes.details:
Your game loop, called once per frame before drawing, with the elapsed seconds (capped at 0.1;
0 until the first frame is on screen, so nothing plays out unseen): read input, spawn, move the
camera. The world (and `overlay`) is stepped for you right after; call `world.update(dt)` here
yourself only to step it at a different point or with a different `dt`.

attributes.name: overlay
attributes.details:
A screen-space layer drawn over the scene by the renderer (scoreboards, buttons): usually a second
`World`, in points from the view's top-left with y up (so on screen y <= 0) and z toward the viewer
within -100..100. Unlit (flat faces show their exact color) and always in front. Stepped each
frame like `source`.

attributes.name: paused
attributes.details: Suspend updates and drawing while keeping the native surface mounted.

attributes.name: quality
attributes.details:
Resolution, anti-aliasing and shadows. "auto" (default) starts at "high", steps down only while
the GPU really can't keep up (crisper shadows, then no shadows or anti-aliasing, resolution last) and
steps back up once frames are smooth again, so every phone gets the best look it can hold.

attributes.name: qualityKey
attributes.details:
Remembers the level "auto" settles on under this key (e.g. the game's id) in the engine's durable
store, so every later view with the same key, after app restarts too, starts there rather than at "high".

attributes.name: source
attributes.details: What to draw (usually a `World`). Changing it restarts the view; never pass a disposed world.

attributes.name: color
attributes.details: CSS color; a `text-*` class takes precedence. Defaults to the current text color.

attributes.name: name
attributes.details: A named icon supplied by the imported entry, or a literal Unicode symbol/emoji.

attributes.name: paths
attributes.details: SVG path data, drawn in order.

attributes.name: size
attributes.details: Square size in logical points. Default: 24.

attributes.name: strokeWidth
attributes.details: Strokes the paths with round caps and joins instead of filling them, in viewBox units.

attributes.name: viewBox
attributes.details: Side of a square viewBox, or `[x, y, width, height]`. Default: 24.

attributes.name: allowDownscaling
attributes.details: Decode near the laid-out size at screen density. Disable for original-resolution pixels.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.details: Prioritize this image once visible. Browser HTML also loads it eagerly at high fetch priority.

attributes.name: recyclingKey
attributes.details: Change to retry a failed source or reset a recycled view.

attributes.name: onKeyPress
attributes.details: Deprecated. Use `onKeyUp` or `onKeyDown` instead

attributes.name: onKeyPressCapture
attributes.details: Deprecated. Use `onKeyUpCapture` or `onKeyDownCapture` instead

attributes.name: keyboardVerticalOffset
attributes.details: Override the automatically measured screen/header offset, in points.

attributes.name: toolbar
attributes.details: Previous, Next and Done controls for engine inputs. Default: true on native.

attributes.name: estimatedItemSize
attributes.details: Rust measures row content when itemSize is omitted.

attributes.name: headerSize
attributes.details: Exact height of the scrolling header in logical points.

attributes.name: itemSize
attributes.details: Exact row height in logical points, including any separator.

attributes.name: onEndReachedThreshold
attributes.details: Distance to the end as a fraction of the viewport height. Default: 0.5.

attributes.name: overscan
attributes.details: Extra rows mounted on each side of the viewport. Default: 6.

attributes.name: refreshControl
attributes.type: ReactElement<{ refreshing?: boolean; onRefresh?: () => void; tintColor?: string; }, string | React.JSXElementConstructor<any>>

attributes.name: separatorSize
attributes.details: Space reserved inside each row for its separator. Default: 1.

attributes.name: stickyHeaderSize
attributes.details: Exact height of the header pinned inside the list viewport.

attributes.name: animating
attributes.details: Show a static ring when false. Reduced-motion preferences are automatic.

attributes.name: fill
attributes.details: Center within the remaining visible area, below any preceding content.

attributes.name: label
attributes.details: Optional caption displayed beneath the ring.

attributes.name: size
attributes.details: Ring diameter in logical points. small=20, medium=32 (default), large=48.

attributes.name: strokeWidth
attributes.details: Optional ring thickness; defaults to 10% of its diameter.

attributes.name: blockSpacing
attributes.details: Space between blocks, in logical pixels.

attributes.name: document
attributes.details: Optional pre-parsed document; the server binding prepares this automatically.

attributes.name: active
attributes.details: Pause the surface while its screen is inactive.

attributes.name: background
attributes.details: Surface clear color; useful for opaque modal content.

attributes.name: safeArea
attributes.details: Protect the end of the page's scroll content. Defaults to true on native.

attributes.name: showsVerticalScrollIndicator
attributes.details: Hide the page's root indicator without disabling scrolling.

attributes.name: id
attributes.details:
Used to locate this view from native classes. Has precedence over `nativeID` prop.

> This disables the 'layout-only view removal' optimization for this view!

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#id

attributes.name: isSelected
attributes.details: Retained selection semantics for engine menu/list controls.

attributes.name: onClick
attributes.details: The action to perform when this `View` is clicked on by a non-touch click, eg. enter key on a hardware keyboard.

attributes.name: accessibilityActions
attributes.type: readonly Readonly<{ name: AccessibilityActionName | string; label?: string | undefined; }>[]
attributes.details: Provides an array of custom actions available for accessibility.

attributes.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
attributes.details:
A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within
this accessibility element are hidden.

attributes.name: accessibilityHint
attributes.details:
An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform
an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the
accessibility label.


See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilityHint

attributes.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
attributes.details: Prevents view from being inverted if set to true and color inversion is turned on.

attributes.name: accessibilityLabel
attributes.details:
Overrides the text that's read by the screen reader when the user interacts
with the element. By default, the label is constructed by traversing all
the children and accumulating all the `Text` nodes separated by space.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel

attributes.name: accessibilityLabelledBy
attributes.details:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

attributes.name: accessibilityLanguage
attributes.details:
Indicates to the accessibility services that the UI component is in
a specific language. The provided string should be formatted following
the BCP 47 specification (https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47).

attributes.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
attributes.details: When `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` is set, this string will be used as title for the large content viewer.

attributes.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
attributes.details:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

attributes.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
attributes.details:
Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing
screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

attributes.name: accessibilityRole
attributes.details: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

attributes.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
attributes.details:
A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer.
Available on iOS 13.0+

attributes.name: accessibilityState
attributes.details: Indicates to accessibility services that UI Component is in a specific State.

attributes.name: accessibilityValue
attributes.type: Readonly<{ min?: number | undefined; max?: number | undefined; now?: number | undefined; text?: string | undefined; }>

attributes.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
attributes.details:
A value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements
within views that are siblings of the receiver.
Default is `false`.

attributes.name: accessible
attributes.details:
When `true`, indicates that the view is an accessibility element.
By default, all the touchable elements are accessible.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessible

attributes.name: android_disableSound
attributes.details: If true, doesn't play Android system sound on press.

attributes.name: android_ripple
attributes.details: Enables the Android ripple effect and configures its properties.

attributes.name: aria-busy
attributes.details:
alias for accessibilityState

see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

attributes.name: aria-hidden
attributes.details:
A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within
this accessibility element are hidden.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#aria-hidden

attributes.name: aria-label
attributes.details:
Alias for accessibilityLabel  https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#accessibilitylabel
https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

attributes.name: aria-labelledby
attributes.details:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

attributes.name: aria-live
attributes.details:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

attributes.name: aria-modal
attributes.details:
The aria-modal attribute indicates content contained within a modal with aria-modal="true"
should be accessible to the user.
Default is `false`.

attributes.name: aria-valuemax
attributes.details:
alias for accessibilityState
It represents textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars.

attributes.name: blockNativeResponder
attributes.details:
Whether to prevent any other native components from becoming responder
while this pressable is responder.

attributes.name: cancelable
attributes.details:
Whether a press gesture can be interrupted by a parent gesture such as a
scroll event. Defaults to true.

attributes.name: collapsable
attributes.details:
Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw
anything may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an
optimization. Set this property to `false` to disable this optimization and
ensure that this `View` exists in the native view hierarchy.

attributes.name: collapsableChildren
attributes.details:
Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed
from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting
`collapsable={false}` on each child.

attributes.name: delayHoverIn
attributes.details: Duration to wait after hover in before calling `onHoverIn`.

attributes.name: delayHoverOut
attributes.details: Duration to wait after hover out before calling `onHoverOut`.

attributes.name: delayLongPress
attributes.details: Duration (in milliseconds) from `onPressIn` before `onLongPress` is called.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.details: Whether the press behavior is disabled.

attributes.name: experimental_accessibilityOrder
attributes.details:
Defines the order in which descendant elements receive accessibility focus.
The elements in the array represent nativeID values for the respective
descendant elements.

attributes.name: focusable
attributes.details: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

attributes.name: hasTVPreferredFocus
attributes.details: Whether to force the Android TV focus engine to move focus to this view. Deprecated. Use `focusable` instead

attributes.name: hitSlop
attributes.details: Additional distance outside of this view in which a press is detected.

attributes.name: importantForAccessibility
attributes.details:
Controls how view is important for accessibility which is if it fires accessibility events
and if it is reported to accessibility services that query the screen.
Works for Android only. See http://developer.android.com/reference/android/R.attr.html#importantForAccessibility for references.

Possible values:
     'auto' - The system determines whether the view is important for accessibility - default (recommended).
     'yes' - The view is important for accessibility.
     'no' - The view is not important for accessibility.
     'no-hide-descendants' - The view is not important for accessibility, nor are any of its descendant views.

attributes.name: nativeID
attributes.details:
Used to locate this view from native classes.

> This disables the 'layout-only view removal' optimization for this view!

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#nativeid

attributes.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
attributes.details:
Whether this `View` needs to be rendered offscreen and composited with an
alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior.
The default (`false`) falls back to drawing the component and its children
with reduced alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element
instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back
with an alpha value. This default may be noticeable and undesired in the
case where the `View` you are setting an opacity on has multiple
overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping `View`s, or text and a
background).

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely
expensive and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is
not turned on by default.

attributes.name: nextFocusDown
attributes.details:
Designates the next view to receive focus when the user navigates down.
The value is the `nativeID` of the target view.

attributes.name: nextFocusForward
attributes.details:
Designates the next view to receive focus when the user navigates
forward. The value is the `nativeID` of the target view.

attributes.name: nextFocusLeft
attributes.details:
Designates the next view to receive focus when the user navigates left.
The value is the `nativeID` of the target view.

attributes.name: nextFocusRight
attributes.details:
Designates the next view to receive focus when the user navigates right.
The value is the `nativeID` of the target view.

attributes.name: nextFocusUp
attributes.details:
Designates the next view to receive focus when the user navigates up.
The value is the `nativeID` of the target view.

attributes.name: onAccessibilityAction
attributes.details:
When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function
when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

attributes.name: onAccessibilityEscape
attributes.details:
When `accessible` is `true`, the system will invoke this function when the
user performs the escape gesture.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onaccessibilityescape

attributes.name: onAccessibilityTap
attributes.details:
When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function
when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onaccessibilitytap

attributes.name: onBlur
attributes.details:
Callback that is called when the view is blurred.

Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

attributes.name: onFocus
attributes.details:
Callback that is called when the view is focused.

Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

attributes.name: onHoverIn
attributes.details: Called when the hover is activated.

attributes.name: onHoverOut
attributes.details: Called when the hover is deactivated.

attributes.name: onLayout
attributes.details: Called when this view's layout changes.

attributes.name: onLongPress
attributes.details: Called if the time after `onPressIn` lasts longer than `delayLongPress`.

attributes.name: onMagicTap
attributes.details:
When `accessible` is `true`, the system will invoke this function when the
user performs the magic tap gesture.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onmagictap

attributes.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
attributes.details:
Does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness? This is called for
every touch move on the `View` when it is not the responder.

`View.props.onMoveShouldSetResponder: (event) => [true | false]`, where
`event` is a synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onmoveshouldsetresponder

attributes.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
attributes.details:
If a parent `View` wants to prevent a child `View` from becoming responder
on a move, it should have this handler which returns `true`.

`View.props.onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture: (event) => [true | false]`,
where `event` is a synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onMoveShouldsetrespondercapture

attributes.name: onPress
attributes.details: Called after `onPressOut`.

attributes.name: onPressIn
attributes.details:
Called immediately when a touch is engaged, before `onPressOut` and
`onPress`.

attributes.name: onPressMove
attributes.details: Called when the press location moves.

attributes.name: onPressOut
attributes.details: Called when a touch is released.

attributes.name: onResponderGrant
attributes.details:
The View is now responding for touch events. This is the time to highlight
and show the user what is happening.

`View.props.onResponderGrant: (event) => {}`, where `event` is a synthetic
touch event as described above.

Return true from this callback to prevent any other native components from
becoming responder until this responder terminates (Android-only).

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onrespondergrant

attributes.name: onResponderMove
attributes.details:
The user is moving their finger.

`View.props.onResponderMove: (event) => {}`, where `event` is a synthetic
touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onrespondermove

attributes.name: onResponderReject
attributes.details:
Another responder is already active and will not release it to that `View`
asking to be the responder.

`View.props.onResponderReject: (event) => {}`, where `event` is a
synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onresponderreject

attributes.name: onResponderRelease
attributes.details:
Fired at the end of the touch.

`View.props.onResponderRelease: (event) => {}`, where `event` is a
synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onresponderrelease

attributes.name: onResponderTerminate
attributes.details:
The responder has been taken from the `View`. Might be taken by other
views after a call to `onResponderTerminationRequest`, or might be taken
by the OS without asking (e.g., happens with control center/ notification
center on iOS)

`View.props.onResponderTerminate: (event) => {}`, where `event` is a
synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onresponderterminate

attributes.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
attributes.details:
Some other `View` wants to become responder and is asking this `View` to
release its responder. Returning `true` allows its release.

`View.props.onResponderTerminationRequest: (event) => {}`, where `event`
is a synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onresponderterminationrequest

attributes.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
attributes.details:
Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

`View.props.onStartShouldSetResponder: (event) => [true | false]`, where
`event` is a synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onstartshouldsetresponder

attributes.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
attributes.details:
If a parent `View` wants to prevent a child `View` from becoming responder
on a touch start, it should have this handler which returns `true`.

`View.props.onStartShouldSetResponderCapture: (event) => [true | false]`,
where `event` is a synthetic touch event as described above.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onstartshouldsetrespondercapture

attributes.name: pointerEvents
attributes.details:
Controls whether the `View` can be the target of touch events.

- `'auto'`: The view can be the target of touch events.
- `'none'`: The view is never the target of touch events.
- `'box-none'`: The view is never the target of touch events but its
  subviews can be.
- `'box-only'`: The view can be the target of touch events but its
  subviews cannot be.

attributes.name: pressRetentionOffset
attributes.details:
Additional distance outside of this view in which a touch is considered a
press before `onPressOut` is triggered.

attributes.name: removeClippedSubviews
attributes.details:
This is a special performance property exposed by `RCTView` and is useful
for scrolling content when there are many subviews, most of which are
offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a
view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound. The
subviews must also have `overflow: hidden`, as should the containing view
(or one of its superviews).

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#removeclippedsubviews

attributes.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
attributes.details:
Whether this `View` should render itself (and all of its children) into a
single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only
modify opacity, rotation, translation and/or scale: in those cases, the
view does not have to be redrawn and display lists do not need to be
re-executed. The texture can be re-used and re-composited with different
parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so
this prop should be set back to `false` at the end of the interaction/
animation.

attributes.name: role
attributes.details: Alias for accessibilityRole

attributes.name: screenReaderFocusable
attributes.details:
Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable. This has lower priority
than focusable or accessible props.

attributes.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
attributes.details:
Whether this `View` should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing.

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not
modify this component's dimensions nor its children; for example, when
translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the
renderer to skip re-rendering the view frame and re-use the cached
bitmap.

Rasterization incurs an offscreen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes
memory. Test and measure when using this property.

attributes.name: tabIndex
attributes.details:
Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.
See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex
for more details.

Supports the following values:
-  0 (View is focusable)
- -1 (View is not focusable)

attributes.name: testID
attributes.details: Identifier used to find this view in tests.

attributes.name: testOnly_pressed
attributes.details: Used only for documentation or testing (e.g. snapshot testing).

attributes.name: unstable_pressDelay
attributes.details:
Duration (in milliseconds) to wait after press down before calling
`onPressIn`.

attributes.name: hitSlop
attributes.details:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.
Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least
30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels.

> The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and the Z-index
> of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch hits two overlapping
> views.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#hitslop

attributes.name: onClick
attributes.details: The action to perform when this `View` is clicked on by a non-touch click, eg. enter key on a hardware keyboard.

attributes.name: onLayout
attributes.details:
Invoked on mount and layout changes with:

`{nativeEvent: { layout: {x, y, width, height}}}`

This event is fired immediately once the layout has been calculated, but
the new layout may not yet be reflected on the screen at the time the
event is received, especially if a layout animation is in progress.

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#onlayout

attributes.name: testID
attributes.details:
Used to locate this view in end-to-end tests.

> This disables the 'layout-only view removal' optimization for this view!

See https://reactnative.dev/docs/view#testid

attributes.name: dynamicTypeRamp

The [Dynamic Type](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uifont/textstyle)
ramp to apply.

attributes.name: ellipsizeMode
attributes.details:
How text is truncated when `numberOfLines` is set. On Android with
`numberOfLines` greater than 1, only `'tail'` works correctly.

attributes.name: lineBreakStrategyIOS
attributes.details: Line break strategy on iOS.

attributes.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
attributes.details:
Largest possible font scale when `allowFontScaling` is enabled.
`null`/`undefined` inherits from the parent node or the global default (0).
`0` means no max (ignores parent/global default). `>= 1` sets the
`maxFontSizeMultiplier` of this node to this value.

attributes.name: minimumFontScale
attributes.details:
Smallest possible font scale when `adjustsFontSizeToFit` is enabled
(values 0.01-1.0).

attributes.name: onPressIn
attributes.details: Called immediately when a touch is engaged.

attributes.name: onTextLayout
attributes.details: Invoked on text layout change.

attributes.name: pressRetentionOffset
attributes.type: Readonly<{ top: number; left: number; bottom: number; right: number; }>
attributes.details:
Defines how far your touch may move off of the button, before
deactivating the button.

attributes.name: selectionColor
attributes.details: Highlight color of the text when selected.

attributes.name: suppressHighlighting
attributes.details:
When `true`, no visual change is made when text is pressed down. By
default, a gray oval highlights the text on press down.

attributes.name: textBreakStrategy
attributes.details: Text break strategy on Android.

attributes.details: Static defaults or a resolver that updates when the active appearance changes.

attributes.details: Initial uncontrolled preference. Root themes default to system; nested themes inherit.

attributes.name: fonts
attributes.details: Root UI typefaces, loaded through engine assets. Native navigation may register the same faces with its platform font loader.

attributes.name: navigation
attributes.details: Restrict this system-bar scope to its focused screen, including frozen screens.

attributes.name: onThemeChange
attributes.details: Observe changes, or update a controlled `theme` preference in the application store.

attributes.name: palette
attributes.details: Shared application tokens. CamelCase color names also configure semantic renderer tokens.

attributes.name: palettes
attributes.details: Light/dark application tokens, resolved with the selected preference.

attributes.name: persistence
attributes.details: Persist and observe the preference in engine storage, independently of account state.

attributes.name: presentationBackground
attributes.details: Platform backdrop for dialogs and sheets that opt in with `blurred`.

attributes.name: presentationInsets
attributes.details: Safe-area values supplied by the host app for modal presentation chrome.

attributes.name: providers
attributes.details: Re-provide app services across the independent Rust UI React renderer.

attributes.name: safeArea
attributes.details: Root themes supply safe-area measurements when no provider already exists. Default: true.

attributes.name: stylesheet
attributes.details: Browser CSS rules compiled to the Rust layout backend.

attributes.name: systemBars
attributes.details: Root themes manage native system bars automatically; nested themes opt in.

attributes.name: textProps
attributes.details: Scoped native text defaults; individual NText props take precedence.

attributes.name: toasts
attributes.details: Root themes manage a lazy toast outlet. Use false for entirely manual hosting.

attributes.name: maxWidth
attributes.details: Centered width limit on tablets and desktop; defaults to 480 points.

attributes.name: top
attributes.details: Absolute top offset. Defaults to the top safe area plus 12 points.

attributes.name: toggleTheme
attributes.details: Switch to the opposite of the currently resolved light/dark appearance.

attributes.name: theme
attributes.details: Selected preference; use resolvedTheme for the active light/dark appearance.

attributes.name: palette
attributes.details: Active application tokens, including camelCase aliases of semantic colors.

attributes.name: colors
attributes.details: Semantic overrides; unspecified colors retain the renderer's defaults.

attributes.name: autoPlay
attributes.details: Start a new source automatically when the platform allows it. Defaults to false.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.details: Show the platform's playback controls. Defaults to true.

attributes.name: playbackRate
attributes.details: Playback speed multiplier from 0.25 to 4. Defaults to 1.

attributes.name: volume
attributes.details: Volume from 0 to 1 where supported. Defaults to 1.

attributes.name: ref
attributes.details:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

attributes.name: aria-activedescendant
attributes.details: Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox, group, or application.

attributes.name: aria-atomic
attributes.details: Indicates whether assistive technologies will present all, or only parts of, the changed region based on the change notifications defined by the aria-relevant attribute.

attributes.name: aria-autocomplete
attributes.details:
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be
presented if they are made.

attributes.name: aria-braillelabel
attributes.details: Defines a string value that labels the current element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

attributes.name: aria-brailleroledescription
attributes.details: Defines a human-readable, author-localized abbreviated description for the role of an element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

attributes.name: aria-colcount
attributes.details: Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-colindex
attributes.details: Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-colindextext
attributes.details: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-colindex.

attributes.name: aria-colspan
attributes.details: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-controls
attributes.details: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

attributes.name: aria-current
attributes.details: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

attributes.name: aria-describedby
attributes.details: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

attributes.name: aria-description
attributes.details: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

attributes.name: aria-details
attributes.details: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

attributes.name: aria-dropeffect
attributes.details: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target. Deprecated. in ARIA 1.1

attributes.name: aria-errormessage
attributes.details: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

attributes.name: aria-flowto
attributes.details:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

attributes.name: aria-grabbed
attributes.details: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation. Deprecated. in ARIA 1.1

attributes.name: aria-haspopup
attributes.details: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

attributes.name: aria-invalid
attributes.details: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

attributes.name: aria-keyshortcuts
attributes.details: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

attributes.name: aria-level
attributes.details: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

attributes.name: aria-multiline
attributes.details: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

attributes.name: aria-multiselectable
attributes.details: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

attributes.name: aria-orientation
attributes.details: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

attributes.name: aria-owns
attributes.details:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

attributes.name: aria-placeholder
attributes.details:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

attributes.name: aria-posinset
attributes.details: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

attributes.name: aria-pressed
attributes.details: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

attributes.name: aria-readonly
attributes.details: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

attributes.name: aria-relevant
attributes.details: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

attributes.name: aria-required
attributes.details: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

attributes.name: aria-roledescription
attributes.details: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

attributes.name: aria-rowcount
attributes.details: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-rowindex
attributes.details: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-rowindextext
attributes.details: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

attributes.name: aria-rowspan
attributes.details: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

attributes.name: aria-setsize
attributes.details: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

attributes.name: aria-sort
attributes.details: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.
